title: Finite geometric sections indexed by closed-point Frobenius orbits
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Use the rationalized/common-stage constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Let $Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], put $Z=Z_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $M$ be a constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf on $Z$, with no Weil structure assumed. Compact cohomology is [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]; its evaluation $e_z:H_c^0(Z,M)\to M_z$ is degree zero of the canonical compact rational counit germ [def-a1-proper-sections-germ-and-moving-point], with $M_z=\mathrm H^0(\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M))$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

For a closed point $x\in|Z_0|$ [def-weil-closed-points], write $d_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]$ using the residue field [def-weil-residue-field], and let $P_x$ consist of $k$-points $z:s\to Z$ projecting to $x$. Then $Z(k)$ and $|Z_0|$ are finite, the projection $Z(k)\to|Z_0|$ is surjective, and $P_x$ is naturally the set of $k_0$-embeddings $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$. In particular $|P_x|=d_x\geq1$.

Put $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{Z_0}\times h$, where $\gamma=(c\mapsto c^q)^{-1}$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. The permutation $T(z)=gzh^{-1}$ of $Z(k)$ preserves every $P_x$, corresponds on embeddings to postcomposition with $\gamma^{-1}$, and is one cycle of length $d_x$ there. Thus $g^{d_x}z=zh^{d_x}$ for $z\in P_x$.

The canonical germ evaluations give a natural $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism
$$e_M:H_c^0(Z,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in|Z_0|}\ \bigoplus_{z\in P_x}M_z.$$
Every $M_z$ and $H_c^0(Z,M)$ is finite-dimensional. Naturality holds for all morphisms of constructible sheaves, without requiring a Weil structure. At $\Qlb$ these maps and spaces are scalar extensions from any common finite coefficient-field stage. These assertions allow nonreduced $Z_0$ and the empty scheme.

Rational/common-stage coefficients as Deligne Weil II (1.1.3); Frobenius convention (1.1.7).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim], write $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ over $k_0$, with $B_0$ finite-dimensional. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] with $R=k_0$: its unique prime is $(0)$, so $Z_0$ has finitely many points, all closed. At its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$, the residue field is $B_0/\mathfrak m_x$: localizing this quotient field changes nothing. It is a nonzero finite-dimensional quotient of $B_0$. Thus $1\le d_x<\infty$, and $\kappa(x)$ is a finite field (a finite basis identifies its underlying set with $k_0^{d_x}$). A finite morphism is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so the proper germ construction in the statement applies.

source.place: Tag 06RS, lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian, first paragraph of proof; finite-algebra specialization

proof.text: The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Z(k)$ with $k_0$-morphisms $s\to Z_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], those with image $x$ correspond exactly to $k_0$-embeddings $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$. An embedding exists by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed], since a finite-dimensional field extension is algebraic. Fix one, $\iota_x$. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], $\kappa(x)/k_0$ is normal and its automorphisms are exactly the $d_x$ distinct powers of $F_x:c\mapsto c^q$. By [lem-sfb-normal-embeddings-automorphism-transitive], all its embeddings into $k$ are exactly $\iota_xF_x^j$ for $0\le j<d_x$. These are distinct because $\iota_x$ is injective. Hence $|P_x|=d_x$, the projection is surjective, and its domain is finite as a finite union of these finite sets.

Use the affine formula for $g$ in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. The point corresponding to an embedding $\iota_x$ is the algebra map $B_0\otimes_{k_0}k\to k$, $b\otimes c\mapsto\iota_x(\bar b)c$. Since $(h^{-1})^*=\gamma^{-1}$, the composite $T(z)=gzh^{-1}$ sends $b\otimes c$ to $\gamma^{-1}(\iota_x(\bar b)\gamma(c))=\gamma^{-1}(\iota_x(\bar b))c$. It is again a $k$-point over $x$ and its embedding is $\gamma^{-1}\iota_x=\iota_xF_x$. On the list in step 2, $T$ is therefore $j\mapsto j+1$ modulo $d_x$. This proves the permutation and single-cycle assertions with the claimed sign. Iterating the defining composite gives $T^r(z)=g^rzh^{-r}$ by cancellation; $T^{d_x}(z)=z$ implies $g^{d_x}z=zh^{d_x}$.

source.place: Corrected geometric evaluation indexing; explicit semilinear coordinate calculation

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ for $B=B_0\otimes_{k_0}k$. The tensors of a $k_0$-basis of $B_0$ with $1$ span $B$ over $k$, so $B$ is module-finite. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] over $k$ gives a finite set $J$ of maximal ideals and their intersection $N=\sqrt{0}$. Each $B/\mathfrak m$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, hence its structural map from $k$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial]. Distinct maximal ideals are comaximal: otherwise their sum would lie in a maximal ideal containing both. Thus [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] gives the canonical quotient-map isomorphism $B/N\simeq\prod_{\mathfrak m\in J}B/\mathfrak m\simeq\prod_{\mathfrak m\in J}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], each such point has exactly one $k$-rational lift, so $J$ identifies canonically with $Z(k)$.

source.place: Tag 06RS, lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian; Tag 00DT, lemma-chinese-remainder (the existing CRT node has a miscited source tag)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $R=\operatorname{Spec}(B/N)$ is canonically $\coprod_{z\in Z(k)}s$. The inclusion of its $z$-component followed by $i:R\to Z$ is the given point $z$, because on rings it is the corresponding residue quotient and its canonical identification with $k$. The quotient map makes $i$ a closed immersion, surjective since $N$ lies in every prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism] to conclude that $i$ is a universal homeomorphism. No reducedness of $Z$ is being assumed. Also $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] (a field has just two ideals), and has dimension zero when nonempty since all primes are maximal. The same assertions hold for $R$ and $s$. These are the finiteness hypotheses needed for the continuous rational realization below.

source.place: Tag 00DT, lemma-chinese-remainder; geometric realization of the quotient by the nilradical

proof.text: First take $\Lambda=E$. Since $Z$ is separated of finite type over $k$, [lem-zl-sf-pbc-normalized-heart-model] applies: the identity-induced equivalence from the sf raw category of the statement to the PBC raw category, followed by the continuous realization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], sends the heart object $M$ to a constructible continuous $E_Z$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ in degree zero. Write $J_Z$ for this composite. The same node identifies the sf pullbacks $Li^*$ and $Lz^*$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with the PBC completed pullbacks, and these are carried, along the closed immersion $i$ and along each closed point $z$, to exact ordinary inverse image, with $i^{-1}E_Z\cong E_R$ and $z^{-1}E_Z\cong E_s$. By [lem-trf-proetale-lower-star-universal-homeomorphism-equivalence] for abelian groups, $i_*$ is an equivalence. Its left adjoint is the $i^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], so its unit $\mathcal F\to i_*i^{-1}\mathcal F$ is invertible. This unit is also module-linear: its action is obtained by applying inverse image to the original scalar-action map and using the displayed coefficient identification. Evaluating at the final object $Z$ therefore gives an $E$-linear natural isomorphism $\mathcal F(Z)\simeq(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(R)$, whose map is restriction along $i$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; formal application of pro-etale topological invariance to continuous coefficient modules

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-coproduct-evaluation] on $R$ to its component open-and-closed immersions $c_z:s\to R$. These are qcqs pro-etale objects, and their coproduct is $R$ itself. It gives $(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(R)\simeq\prod_{z\in Z(k)}(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(s,c_z)$, with component the restriction to the $z$-th component. By the site-object clause of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], $(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(s,c_z)$ is the space of sections over the final object of the exact site restriction $c_z^{-1}i^{-1}\mathcal F$, with $c_z^{-1}E_R=E_s$; since $ic_z=z$ by step 5, its composition comparison identifies this with $(z^{-1}\mathcal F)(s)$. The underlying bijection is a linear isomorphism because restrictions preserve addition and the coefficient action. In combination with step 6 this is a natural linear isomorphism from $\mathcal F(Z)$ to the finite product of its point sections, with its actual restriction components.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; finite disjoint-cover sheaf axiom, with the canonical evaluation components

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-adic-compactification-section-realization] with $T=U=Z$ and $j=\mathrm{id}$, and separately with $T=U=s$. These proper schemes satisfy its hypotheses by steps 1 and 4. Its normalized degree-zero formulas, followed by the fully faithful realization $J$ of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], identify $H_c^0(Z,M)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(E_Z,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(Z)$ and, by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $M_z=H^0(s,Lz^*M)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(E_s,z^{-1}\mathcal F)=(z^{-1}\mathcal F)(s)$. The elementary Hom-to-sections identifications send a module map to the image of $1$, with inverse $t\mapsto(a\mapsto at)$ on each site object. By [lem-zl-sf-pbc-normalized-heart-model] and step 6, $J_s(Lz^*M)\cong z^{-1}\mathcal F$ is a sheaf in degree zero; as that node identifies the sf and PBC standard halves, $Lz^*M$ lies in the heart of $s$. Thus the source and factors of step 7 are exactly the spaces in the question.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; degree-zero unit-Hom formulas at the identity compactifications

proof.text: Check the maps, not only the objects. By [def-a1-proper-sections-germ-and-moving-point], $e_z$ is proper coincidence followed by $Lz^*$ of the specified counit and the inverse comparison for $a_Zz=\mathrm{id}_s$. The system realization [def-weil-system-operation-exchange-realization] retains the normalized ordinary units and counits. Its pullbacks are the sf pullbacks, which [lem-zl-sf-pbc-normalized-heart-model] identifies with the PBC completed pullbacks with the identity integral normalization on the whole finite-reduction diagram, compatibly with identities and composition. By [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization], $J$ carries this adjunction, with its actual counit, to the ambient module adjunction. In that adjunction the counit takes a section pulled back from $a_{Z*}\mathcal F$ to its restriction in $\mathcal F$; pulling it to $z$ sends $t$ to $t|_z$. The identity and composition comparisons in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] identify the source with the same section $t$, with no scalar change. The proper comparison is the identity-compactification comparison fixed in [def-a1-proper-sections-germ-and-moving-point]. Consequently the composite of steps 6-8 has component exactly $e_z$. Reindex its finite product by the partition $Z(k)=\coprod_x P_x$ of step 2 and use the finite product/direct sum identification. This proves the asserted $e_M$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15: ambient adjunction; normalized whole-system and rational comparisons, evaluated on a section

proof.text: Each $M_z=H^0(\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M))$ is finite-dimensional, since $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ takes values in complexes with finite-dimensional cohomology by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; so is $H_c^0(Z,M)$ by the finite direct sum just proved. Restriction of sections commutes with every module-sheaf map, and all comparisons in steps 6-9 are natural, so $e$ is natural for every morphism of constructible sheaves. For a finite coefficient-field extension the section comparisons of [lem-a1-adic-compactification-section-realization] and the point-realization comparisons $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\mathcal H^0-)\cong H^0\operatorname{Fib}_s(-)$ of [lem-a1-point-realization-standard-cohomology] commute with scalar extension; the actual adjunction comparisons commute with it by [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization]. Hence the entire evaluation map, with its specified germ components, extends by scalars. In the common-stage category of [def-weil-constructible-heart], choose any stage representing the object and any common stage representing a morphism. Tensoring the finite-stage isomorphism with $\Qlb$ proves the assertion there and its naturality, independently of the chosen stage. No Weil map has entered the construction. For the empty scheme, the empty-cover sheaf axiom in step 7 makes sections zero and the product/direct sum empty, so the conclusion remains valid.
